title: Reports similar pieces of code.
summary: It is an experimental (alpha) checker, so the analyzer does not run it by default. It applies to C, C++, Objective-C.

title: Similarly to alpha.unix.PthreadLock <alpha-unix-PthreadLock>, checks for the locking/unlocking of mtx_t mutexes.
summary: It is an experimental (alpha) checker, so the analyzer does not run it by default.

title: Check for cast from non-struct pointer to struct pointer.
summary: It is an experimental (alpha) checker, so the analyzer does not run it by default. It applies to C, C++.

title: Loss of sign/precision in implicit conversions.
summary: It is an experimental (alpha) checker, so the analyzer does not run it by default. It applies to C, C++, Objective-C.

title: Check for dereferences of pointers that refer to an object whose lifetime has already ended.
summary: Such a pointer is dangling. The checker reports it when it is dereferenced and when it is passed to a function. It is an experimental (alpha) checker, so the analyzer does not run it by default. It applies to C, C++.

title: Check if a value of active type is retrieved from an std::variant instance with std::get.
summary: In case of bad variant type access (the accessed type differs from the active type) a warning is emitted. Currently, this checker does not take exception handling into account. It is an experimental (alpha) checker, so the analyzer does not run it by default. It applies to C++.

title: Check for writes to immutable memory regions.
summary: This implements part of SEI CERT Rule ENV30-C. It is an experimental (alpha) checker, so the analyzer does not run it by default. It applies to C, C++.

title: Check for returned pointers and references that are bound to an object whose lifetime ends when the function returns.
summary: The checker only analyzes code that is annotated with the [[clang::lifetimebound]] attribute. The annotation tells the checker which object the returned value is bound to. It is an experimental (alpha) checker, so the analyzer does not run it by default. It applies to C, C++.

title: Reports destructions of polymorphic objects with a non-virtual destructor in their base class.
summary: It is an experimental (alpha) checker, so the analyzer does not run it by default. It applies to C++.

title: Check for use of invalidated iterators.
summary: It is an experimental (alpha) checker, so the analyzer does not run it by default. It applies to C++.

title: Check for iterators used outside their valid ranges.
summary: It is an experimental (alpha) checker, so the analyzer does not run it by default. It applies to C++.

title: Check for use of iterators of different containers where iterators of the same container are expected.
summary: It is an experimental (alpha) checker, so the analyzer does not run it by default. It applies to C++.

title: Check for dereference of null smart pointers.
summary: It is an experimental (alpha) checker, so the analyzer does not run it by default. It applies to C++.

title: Check unreachable code.
summary: It is an experimental (alpha) checker, so the analyzer does not run it by default. It applies to C, C++.

title: Similarly to alpha.unix.PthreadLock <alpha-unix-PthreadLock>, checks for the locking/unlocking of fuchsia mutexes.
summary: It is an experimental (alpha) checker, so the analyzer does not run it by default.

title: Check code for LLVM codebase conventions.
summary: It is an experimental (alpha) checker, so the analyzer does not run it by default.

title: Check for local variables, member variables, and function arguments that are forward declared.
summary: It is an experimental (alpha) checker, so the analyzer does not run it by default.

title: Check for all casts from a base type to its derived type as these might be memory-unsafe.
summary: It is an experimental (alpha) checker, so the analyzer does not run it by default.

title: Check that [[clang::annotate_type("webkit.nodelete")]] annotation does not appear on a function which could delete an object.
summary: It is an experimental (alpha) checker, so the analyzer does not run it by default.

title: Raw pointers and references to an object which supports CheckedPtr or CheckedRef can't be used as class members.
summary: Only CheckedPtr, CheckedRef, RefPtr, or Ref are allowed. It is an experimental (alpha) checker, so the analyzer does not run it by default.

title: Raw pointers and references to a NS or CF object can't be used as class members or ivars.
summary: Only RetainPtr is allowed for CF types regardless of whether ARC is enabled or disabled. Only RetainPtr or OSObjectPtr is allowed for NS types when ARC is disabled. It is an experimental (alpha) checker, so the analyzer does not run it by default.

title: The same rule as alpha.webkit.UnborrowedLocalVarsChecker, applied to function arguments.
summary: It is an experimental (alpha) checker, so the analyzer does not run it by default.

title: The same rule as alpha.webkit.UnborrowedLocalVarsChecker, applied to lambda captures.
summary: It is an experimental (alpha) checker, so the analyzer does not run it by default.

title: A *CanBorrow* type tracks views into its interior at runtime.
summary: It calls crashIfBorrowed() in methods that destroy its interior. WTF::Vector is a motivating example: append() calls crashIfBorrowed(). It is an experimental (alpha) checker, so the analyzer does not run it by default.

title: The goal of this rule is to make sure that lifetime of any dynamically allocated CheckedPtr capable object passed as a call argument keeps its memory region past the end of the call.
summary: This applies to call to any function, method, lambda, function pointer or functor. CheckedPtr capable objects aren't supposed to be allocated on stack so we check arguments for parameters of raw pointers and references to unchecked types. It is an experimental (alpha) checker, so the analyzer does not run it by default.

title: Raw pointers and references to unchecked types can't be captured in lambdas.
summary: Only CheckedPtr or CheckedRef is allowed. It is an experimental (alpha) checker, so the analyzer does not run it by default.

title: The goal of this rule is to make sure that any unchecked local variable is backed by a CheckedPtr or CheckedRef with lifetime that is strictly larger than the scope of the unchecked local variable.
summary: To be on the safe side we require the scope of an unchecked variable to be embedded in the scope of CheckedPtr/CheckRef object that backs it. It is an experimental (alpha) checker, so the analyzer does not run it by default.

title: The goal of this rule is to make sure that lifetime of any dynamically allocated ref-countable object passed as a call argument spans past the end of the call.
summary: This applies to call to any function, method, lambda, function pointer or functor. Ref-countable types aren't supposed to be allocated on stack so we check arguments for parameters of raw pointers and references to uncounted types. It is an experimental (alpha) checker, so the analyzer does not run it by default.

title: The goal of this rule is to make sure that any uncounted local variable is backed by a ref-counted object with lifetime that is strictly larger than the scope of the uncounted local variable.
summary: To be on the safe side we require the scope of an uncounted variable to be embedded in the scope of ref-counted object that backs it. It is an experimental (alpha) checker, so the analyzer does not run it by default.

title: The goal of this rule is to make sure that lifetime of any dynamically allocated NS or CF objects passed as a call argument keeps its memory region past the end of the call.
summary: This applies to call to any function, method, lambda, function pointer or functor. NS or CF objects aren't supposed to be allocated on stack so we check arguments for parameters of raw pointers and references to unretained types. It is an experimental (alpha) checker, so the analyzer does not run it by default.

title: Raw pointers and references to NS or CF types can't be captured in lambdas.
summary: Only RetainPtr is allowed for CF types regardless of whether ARC is enabled or disabled, and only RetainPtr or OSObjectPtr is allowed for NS types when ARC is disabled. It is an experimental (alpha) checker, so the analyzer does not run it by default.

title: The goal of this rule is to make sure that any NS or CF local variable is backed by a RetainPtr or OSObjectPtr with lifetime that is strictly larger than the scope of the unretained local variable.
summary: To be on the safe side we require the scope of an unretained variable to be embedded in the scope of RetainPtr or OSObjectPtr object that backs it. It is an experimental (alpha) checker, so the analyzer does not run it by default.

title: Finds ID-dependent variables and fields that are used within loops.
summary: This causes branches to occur inside the loops, and thus leads to performance degradation. The check is in the altera module of clang-tidy.

title: Finds kernel files and include directives whose filename is kernel.cl, Verilog.cl, or VHDL.cl.
summary: The check is case insensitive. The check is in the altera module of clang-tidy.

title: Finds OpenCL kernel functions that call a barrier function but do not call an ID function (get_local_id, get_local_id, get_group_id, or get_local_linear_id).
summary: The check is in the altera module of clang-tidy.

title: Finds structs that are inefficiently packed or aligned, and recommends packing and/or aligning of said structs as needed.
summary: clang-tidy can fix the code that it finds. The check is in the altera module of clang-tidy.

title: Finds inner loops that have not been unrolled, as well as fully unrolled loops with unknown loop bounds or a large number of iterations.
summary: The check is in the altera module of clang-tidy.
